skill.name: helpdesk-automation
skill.description: Automate read-only HelpDesk workflows through Rube MCP. List tickets, views, canned responses, and custom fields with current tool schemas.
skill.summary: Automate read-only HelpDesk ticket discovery and account metadata review through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The command-execution findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around MCP tool names, parameters, and examples. The only confirmed issue is a low-severity external MCP endpoint dependency; no prompt injection, hidden executable code, or system reconnaissance evidence was found.

remediation.suggestion: Document that HelpDesk ticket and account metadata may pass through Rube MCP, and advise users to review Rube and HelpDesk permissions before connecting.

static_findings.snippet: - Active HelpDesk connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `helpdesk`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `HELPDESK_LIST_TICKETS` - List tickets with sorting and pagination [Required]
- Forward pagination requires both `next.value` and `next.ID` from previous response
- `silo` determines which folder to list from; default is active tickets
- Response data may be nested under `data` or `data.data`
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Keep page sizes reasonable to avoid timeouts

content.value_statement: Support teams need fast access to tickets, views, templates, and fields. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists HelpDesk tickets by silo, sort field, order, page size, and cursor values.
Lists saved HelpDesk views used by agents to organize tickets.
Retrieves canned response templates for support reply review.
Lists custom field definitions, field types, names, and validation details.
Checks Rube MCP availability and HelpDesk connection status before workflows.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active HelpDesk connection.
Documented workflows are read-only and do not create, update, or reply to tickets.
Cannot create or modify views, canned responses, or custom fields.
Depends on current Rube tool schemas and available HelpDesk toolkit operations.

use_cases.title: Review Current Ticket Queues
use_cases.description: List active, archived, trash, or spam tickets with predictable sorting and cursor pagination.

use_cases.title: Inspect HelpDesk Configuration
use_cases.description: Review saved views and custom fields to understand how the account organizes support work.

use_cases.title: Audit Response Templates
use_cases.description: Retrieve canned responses and identify templates that need placeholder or formatting review.

prompt_templates.title: List Recent Tickets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Rube MCP to list the newest 20 active HelpDesk tickets. Confirm the HelpDesk connection first and summarize requester, subject, and last update.

prompt_templates.title: Browse a Ticket Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: List 50 archived HelpDesk tickets sorted by updatedAt descending. Use cursor pagination when more results are available.

prompt_templates.title: Review Canned Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve all HelpDesk canned responses. Identify templates with placeholders, HTML formatting, or unclear reply language. Do not send any replies.

prompt_templates.title: Map Support Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the HelpDesk connection, then list views, canned responses, and custom fields. Explain how each item supports triage and response consistency.

output_examples.input: List the newest active tickets and show whether more pages are available.
output_examples.output: A concise ticket summary with IDs, requester details, timestamps, and a note about the next cursor pair.

output_examples.input: Review canned responses for placeholder usage.
output_examples.output: A plain-language template review that flags placeholders, formatting notes, and responses needing support team review.

output_examples.input: Show custom field definitions for the HelpDesk account.
output_examples.output: A field inventory with names, types, validation details, and notes about how fields support ticket routing.

best_practices: Call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS first so tool names and schemas match the current MCP server.
Use both cursor value and cursor ID when moving through ticket pages.
Treat ticket content, custom fields, and response templates as sensitive support data.
anti_patterns: Do not assume tool schemas from memory when Rube MCP can return current schemas.
Do not mix forward and backward cursors in the same ticket request.
Do not query trash or spam silos unless the user explicitly requests those folders.

faq.question: Does this skill require Rube MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. Rube MCP must be configured, and the HelpDesk connection must be active.

faq.question: Can it create or update tickets?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows list tickets and account metadata only.

faq.question: Can it send canned responses?
faq.answer: No. It can list canned responses, but it does not send replies.

faq.question: How does ticket pagination work?
faq.answer: It uses cursor pairs. Pass both the timestamp value and ticket ID from the previous response.

faq.question: Which ticket folders can it list?
faq.answer: It can list active tickets, archive, trash, or spam when the user selects a silo.

faq.question: Is HelpDesk data sent to a third party?
faq.answer: The workflows depend on Rube MCP and the connected HelpDesk account. Review your Rube and HelpDesk permissions.
